text: Yes, tree-cover loss on this property has been increasing in recent years. Between 2021 and 2023, the annual loss rose from 81.3 hectares to 4.5 hectares, though 2022 saw a much smaller loss of 0.6 hectares. The 2021 loss was particularly significant, accounting for 2.23% of the property. While 2022 showed a sharp decline, the upward trend resumed in 2023. These figures exclude smaller patches under 0.5 hectares, which also increased in 2021 (37.3 ha) before dropping in subsequent years. The data suggests fluctuating but generally rising tree-cover loss, with 2021 being the most impactful year.
